citation: IRS Pub. 1345 (Rev. 12-2025), Reporting of Security Incidents (N54-R03)
trigger: Any event that can result in unauthorized disclosure, misuse, modification, or destruction of taxpayer information
deadline: As soon as possible but not later than the next business day after confirmation of the incident
notify: IRS. An ERO-only provider contacts its local Stakeholder Liaison, following the Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals instructions
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. ERO with 6 EFINs. Applies to both runbooks whenever taxpayer information may be affected

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance, not a regulation) (N54-R03)
trigger: Client data stolen or accessed by an unauthorized person
deadline: As quickly as possible ("Speed is critical"); in practice the same call as the Pub. 1345 report
notify: Local IRS Stakeholder Liaison, who notifies IRS Criminal Investigation and others in the IRS
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance)
trigger: Data theft affecting clients for whom the Company prepares state returns
deadline: As quickly as possible, alongside the IRS report
notify: Each state tax agency where affected clients file, using the Federation of Tax Administrators contact list
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Florida has no personal income tax; clients file in many other states

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance); OFAC advisory (reporting as a mitigating factor)
trigger: Data theft, refund or payment diversion, ransomware, or extortion
deadline: As soon as possible after declaration
notify: FBI field office or IC3; local police report; Secret Service if directed
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Also supports the Florida no-harm consultation and any law enforcement delay request
owner: Director of Information Security through counsel

trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information of at least 500 consumers without authorization. Unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise (314.2(m))
deadline: As soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, electronically on the ftc.gov form. Content: name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; any written law enforcement determination (314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more consumers. Count individual clients (consumers), not business entities
clock_starts: Discovery: first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent other than the attacker (314.4(j)(2))

trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public disclosure would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days on written request
notify: Include the determination and the official's contact in the FTC notice
applies_at_this_tier: If requested. It delays the FTC's public disclosure, not the Company's 30-day filing

trigger: Breach of security: unauthorized access of electronic personal information, including name with SSN, name with a financial account number and access code, and a user name or email with its password
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15 more days for good cause shown in writing to the Department within 30 days; individuals only)
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email. Content: date or date range, description of the information, Company contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Worked example for the state notices
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Department of Legal Affairs. Content: synopsis, number of Floridians, services offered, copy of the individual notice, Company contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies: timing, distribution, and content of the notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the Company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for either runbook: stolen tax documents are used for refund fraud. Counsel decides

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines notice to individuals would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: If requested

trigger: Notice given under the rules of the Company's primary or functional federal regulator
deadline: Deemed compliant if individuals are notified under those rules and the Department timely receives a copy
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No for the Company's own customers. The FTC Safeguards Rule requires notice to the FTC only, not to individuals, so there is no federal individual notice to rely on. Counsel confirms

obligation: Service provider breach notice to the Company (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent (tax software, portal, cloud, payroll, offshore vendor)
deadline: Provider notifies the Company as expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination
notify: The Company, which then gives the (3) and (4) notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Opens an incident under POL-03 4.12

obligation: Company as third-party agent to CAS clients (outbound)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a) and (1)(h); CAS client agreements
trigger: Breach of a Company system that maintains client employees' or payees' personal information for a CAS client
deadline: No later than 10 days after determination (Florida); sooner if the CAS agreement says so (72 hours in the current template)
notify: Each affected CAS client, which as the covered entity gives its own notices; the Company may notify on the client's behalf only by agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. About 210 payroll clients and 340 bookkeeping clients

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, and territories)
trigger: Affected individuals who reside outside Florida (about 19% of individual clients, plus out-of-state client employees)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents, and state attorneys general or regulators where each state requires; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; counsel builds the list from addresses

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance)
trigger: Client data theft
deadline: Work with law enforcement on timing; combine with the state notices
notify: Letter to each victim. Clients file Form 14039 only if they receive an IRS notice or an e-filed return is rejected for a duplicate SSN; recommend an IRS Identity Protection PIN
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Business associate breach notice to covered entity
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held for a health care client
deadline: Without unreasonable delay, no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, or the shorter BAA term (5 to 10 business days in 11 of 44 BAAs)
notify: Each affected covered entity client: identity of affected individuals and the information it needs for its own notices (164.410(c))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Business associate for 44 health care clients
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known to any employee, officer, or agent other than the person committing the breach (164.410(a)(2))

trigger: Any security incident involving ePHI held for a covered entity client, including breaches of unsecured PHI
deadline: Per each BAA
notify: Covered entity client
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Contract terms tracked in the contract register

trigger: Incident affecting a client's confidential engagement data (workpapers, SOC evidence)
deadline: Per engagement letter; target within 72 hours of confirmation
notify: Engagement partner calls the client
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Contractual, not legal

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy. Call the carrier hotline before engaging incident vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline ($15 million limit, $500,000 retention)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Contractual, not legal

trigger: Material disruption or cyber event as the agreements define it
deadline: Per agreement
notify: Administrative agent; sponsor operating partner; board and audit committee chairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. CFO and General Counsel decide

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion or ransom demand is considered for payment
deadline: Before any payment. Full and timely reporting to law enforcement is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a payment is considered (POL-03 4.9)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No. Final rule not published as of 2026-09-25, so reporting is not required. The Company exceeds its SBA size standard, so counsel will reassess when a final rule is published

citation: Form 8-K Item 1.05; Regulation S-K Item 106 (17 CFR 229.106)
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public company
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining materiality
notify: SEC
applies_at_this_tier: No. The Company is privately held and has no registered securities

trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
notify: DoD through https://dibnet.dod.mil
applies_at_this_tier: No. No federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Covered telecommunications equipment or services found in use
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification, then a further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No. Only if the Company holds federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Covered article (Kaspersky Lab products or services) found in use
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification, then a further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No. Only if the Company holds federal contracts or subcontracts
